lines.text: Your fingers aren't just soaking up water.
Your nervous system is actively changing them.
After staying submerged for several minutes,
your nervous system sends tiny electrical signals
down beneath the skin of your fingertips.
Those signals actively narrow tiny blood vessels below.
As blood volume drops inside the fingertip,
the outer skin pulls inward, forming wrinkles.
Scientists tested whether these ridges channel water away,
helping your fingers grip wet objects underwater—
though researchers still debate how consistently that helps.
Either way, your body may adapt its grip
much more cleverly than you think.
